ML.0: a normalisation registry (Art_K, rec_K, rec^T_K, Hodge-Tate sign, r_{pi,iota}, meaning of 'Sym^{n-1} pi exists') checked against Newton-Thorne and ACC+. nodes.title: The common normalisations of Artin maps, local Langlands, Hodge-Tate weights and r_{pi,iota} used by the modularity endpoints
nodes.statement: The endpoint sources Newton-Thorne I-II and ACC+ use one set of conventions, which this registry fixes for every ML stage. (a) Local class field theory is normalised cohomologically: Art_K: K^x -> W_K^ab sends uniformisers to geometric Frobenius elements, and Frob_v denotes a geometric Frobenius lift. (b) rec_K is the Harris-Taylor local Langlands correspondence for GL_n(K), a bijection from irreducible admissible C[GL_n(K)]-modules to Frobenius-semisimple Weil-Deligne representations of rank n. rec^T_K is its Tate (arithmetic) normalisation of [CT14, §2.1]; over C, rec^T_K(pi) = rec_K(pi ⊗ |.|^{(1-n)/2}). (c) Hodge-Tate weights are normalised so that the cyclotomic character has Hodge-Tate weight -1. (d) If pi is cuspidal, regular algebraic and polarizable (in the sense of BLGGT14) over a CM or totally real field F, then for every isomorphism iota: Qbar_p -> C there is a continuous semisimple r_{pi,iota}: G_F -> GL_n(Qbar_p) with WD(r_{pi,iota}|G_{F_v})^{F-ss} ≅ rec^T_{F_v}(iota^{-1} pi_v) at every finite place v. (e) For n = 2, 'weight k' means the infinitesimal character of (⊗_tau Sym^{k-2} C^2)^dual. Then r_{pi,iota} has Hodge-Tate weights {0, k-1} at every embedding, and epsilon^{k-1} det r_{pi,iota} has finite order. (f) 'Sym^{n-1} pi exists' means there is a cuspidal automorphic Pi_n of GL_n(A_F) with rec_{F_v}(Pi_{n,v}) ≅ Sym^{n-1} ∘ rec_{F_v}(pi_v) at every place v (Newton-Thorne Hilbert, Theorem A; the source prints rec_{F_v}(Pi_n)). Newton-Thorne II Theorem A.1 uses the same phrase for an isobaric, usually non-cuspidal, Pi_n; there cuspidality is dropped. The Galois-side statement 'Sym^{n-1} r_{pi,iota} is automorphic' is not defined in the Notation sections read; this registry reads it as r_{Pi,iota} ≅ Sym^{n-1} r_{pi,iota} for a regular algebraic cuspidal Pi under convention (d) (compare BLGGT14 §2.1 and ACC+ §7.1 for the source definitions of automorphy of Galois representations and systems).
hypotheses: Conventions (d) and (e) are stated for cuspidal, regular algebraic, polarizable pi over CM or totally real F. Newton-Thorne attribute the existence of r_{pi,iota} and its compatibility with rec^T at every finite place to the literature with '(see e.g. [Car14])' ([Car14] = Caraiani, Monodromy and local-global compatibility for l = p). The registry does not assert Galois representations for non-polarizable or non-regular pi.

ACC+ Theorem 2.3.3 (§2.3.1; arXiv v2 pp. 39-40) is weaker. It concerns a xi-cohomological cuspidal pi on ACC+'s quasi-split unitary group G~ (rank 2n) over a CM field F containing an imaginary quadratic field F_0, and gives a 2n-dimensional r_iota(pi). It proves the Weil-Deligne identification (its condition (c)) only at places above primes l that split in F_0. Its conditions (a)-(b) cover Frobenius polynomials at primes l != p unramified in F and for pi, and de Rham-ness with the stated Hodge-Tate numbers at p. It is not the full local-global compatibility of convention (d).
rec_K is Harris-Taylor's correspondence [HT01]. Identifying it with any other construction of the local correspondence needs a separate characterisation theorem.
proofSteps: Newton-Thorne II, Notation (pp. 3-5): cohomological normalisation of Art_K; rec_K and rec^T_K with rec^T_K(pi) = rec_K(pi ⊗ |.|^{(1-n)/2}) over C; existence of r_{pi,iota} for cuspidal regular algebraic polarizable pi with local-global compatibility at all finite places (citing [Car14]); Hodge-Tate weight of the cyclotomic character is -1; the weight-k convention for n = 2.
Newton-Thorne I, Notation (pp. 6-7), gives the same conventions and defines Sp_n(psi), St_n(psi) with rec^T_K(St_n(psi)) = Sp_n(psi).

ACC+ §1.2 (pp. 906-907): Art_K sends uniformisers to geometric Frobenius; rec_K is the correspondence of [HT01]; rec^T_K is the arithmetic normalisation of [CT14, §2.1]; HT_tau(epsilon_p) = {-1}. The conventions agree with Newton-Thorne's.
Newton-Thorne Hilbert, Theorem A (p. 1), fixes the meaning of the existence of Sym^{n-1} pi through rec_{F_v}(Pi_n) ≅ Sym^{n-1} ∘ rec_{F_v}(pi_v) at every place v.
acceptance: Check the twist compatibility implied by (b) and (f). With rec^T = rec ⊗ |.|^{(1-m)/2} in rank m, Sym^{n-1}(rec^T_{F_v}(pi_v)) and rec^T_{F_v}(Pi_n) must agree. This follows from Sym^{n-1}(rec(pi_v) ⊗ |.|^{-1/2}) = Sym^{n-1}(rec(pi_v)) ⊗ |.|^{-(n-1)/2}. Record this computation as a checked lemma, not a source quotation.
Check that Frob_v in every Galois-side characteristic polynomial is geometric, consistent with Art_K. A consumer using arithmetic Frobenius must convert explicitly.
Check the sign convention on the cyclotomic character, HT(epsilon) = -1, for weight 2: HT weights {0, 1} and det r = epsilon^{-1}, as in Newton-Thorne II §2, condition (7).
Every endpoint node of this roadmap cites which part of (a)-(f) it uses.

nodes.title: Corollary 10.2(ii) of KW I: continuous odd irreducible rho: G_Q -> GL_2(C) arises from a weight-one newform (Artin and Langlands conjectures in this case)
nodes.statement: Khare-Wintenberger I, Corollary 10.2(ii): a continuous, odd, irreducible representation rho: G_Q -> GL_2(C) arises from a newform of weight one. The source deduces from Theorem 10.1(ii) that Langlands' conjecture holds for such rho, and hence Artin's conjecture: L(rho, s) extends to an entire function, by Godement-Jacquet. Together with Deligne-Serre, which attaches such representations to weight-one newforms, this characterises the odd irreducible two-dimensional complex representations of G_Q as those attached to weight-one newforms. The new cases are those with non-solvable projective image, isomorphic to A_5. Solvable projective image was earlier covered by Langlands [31] and Tunnell [45]. The statement concerns G_Q only. It gives no weight-one modularity over other number fields.
hypotheses: rho is continuous, odd (det rho(c) = -1 for complex conjugation c) and irreducible, with values in GL_2(C). Its image is then finite.

The source derives this from Theorem 10.1(ii), whose proof is only sketched there. It uses Serre's conjecture in infinitely many residue characteristics (KW I Theorems 1.2 and 9.1, and Theorem 0.1 and Corollary 0.2 of [28]). The source says the proof of Theorem 10.1 'is similar to the arguments in Sections 4.7 and 4.8 of [38]' (Serre, Duke Math. J. 54 (1987)) and also uses the argument of [21]; Serre §§4.7-4.8 was not read.

Theorem 10.1(ii) also uses the Sen-Fontaine unramifiedness theorem and the Gross [19] and Coleman-Voloch [7] weight-one arguments, via Khare [21] and Edixhoven [14] §3.4. The source cites these without proof.
proofSteps: Theorem 10.1(ii) (KW I, p. 20; decomposed in ClassicalSerreModularity:R27.6): a two-dimensional irregular compatible system that is irreducible and odd arises up to twist from a newform of weight 1. The sketched proof first shows that rho-bar_lambda is irreducible for almost all lambda, because the conductor is bounded and the Hodge-Tate weights are fixed. It twists to Hodge-Tate numbers (0, 0) and uses Sen-Fontaine: rho_lambda is unramified at the residue characteristic of lambda for all but finitely many lambda. Serre's conjecture with [21], [19], [7] then puts rho-bar_lambda, for almost all lambda, in S_1(Gamma_1(N)) with N independent of lambda.

§10.2 (p. 21): 'Part (ii) of Theorem 10.1 implies Langlands' conjecture, and hence that of Artin, for odd, irreducible, complex representations rho: G_Q -> GL_2(C).' Artin's conjecture follows from Langlands' because L(pi, s) is entire by Godement-Jacquet [18].

The passage from an Artin representation rho to an irregular, irreducible, odd compatible system, and the removal of the 'up to twist', are not written out in the source. They are recorded as a gap, not supplied here.

The source contrasts this with Deligne-Serre [10], which attaches odd irreducible complex representations to weight-one newforms, and with the solvable-image cases of Langlands [31] and Tunnell [45]. Only projective image A_5 is new.
acceptance: The statement is over Q only. The node must not be cited for weight-one modularity over totally real or CM fields.
The weight-one representation is complex with finite image. The node must not derive it from a weight-two Jacobian or an l-adic Tate module.

Example check: for a rho with projective image A_5, the newform produced has weight 1 and nebentypus det rho, and its level is the Artin conductor. Level and character must be verified separately. The source proves only 'arises from'.
The solvable-image input (Langlands-Tunnell) is not used by this deduction. Do not add it as a prerequisite without a source location in the proof.

nodes.title: Corollary 10.2(i) of KW I: abelian varieties of GL_2-type over Q are quotients of J_1(N)
nodes.statement: Khare-Wintenberger I, Corollary 10.2(i). An abelian variety A over Q of GL_2-type is modular, i.e. isomorphic to a quotient of J_1(N) for some N. GL_2-type means: A is simple, and End_Q(A) ⊗ Q contains a number field E with [E:Q] = dim A (Ribet's primitive GL_2-type). The source states that N may be taken to be M^n, with M the conductor and n the dimension of A (terminology from Ribet [33]). The source obtains the result by combining Theorem 10.1(i) with Faltings' isogeny theorem, referring to Theorem 4.4 of Ribet [33]. The result is over Q only. It does not cover elliptic curves or GL_2-type abelian varieties over other number fields.
hypotheses: A is an abelian variety over Q, simple, with a number field E ⊂ End_Q(A) ⊗ Q of degree dim A.

Theorem 10.1(i) is used for the regular, irreducible, odd compatible system of E_lambda-adic Tate modules of A. The source does not show that this system has these properties; it refers to Ribet [33].
Faltings' isogeny theorem is used to pass from equality of compatible systems to an isogeny, hence a quotient of J_1(N).
proofSteps: Theorem 10.1(i) (KW I p. 20; ClassicalSerreModularity:R27.6): a two-dimensional regular irreducible odd compatible system arises up to twist from a newform of weight >= 2.
§10.2 (p. 21): 'Part (i) of Theorem 10.1 combined with Faltings' isogeny theorem yields modularity of abelian varieties of GL_2-type over Q (see Theorem 4.4 of [33]).'
The source states that simple quotients of J_1(N) over Q are of GL_2-type, and defines 'modular' as isomorphic to a quotient of J_1(N) with N = M^n.

The intermediate steps (the system of V_lambda(A) is weight two, regular, odd and irreducible; A is isogenous to the Shimura quotient A_f; isogeny to isomorphism) are in Ribet [33] Theorem 4.4, which was not read.
acceptance: The output is 'isomorphic to a quotient of J_1(N)' over Q. A parametrisation X_1(N) -> A needs a further argument and is not supplied here.
Example check: for an elliptic curve E/Q (n = 1, E = Q), N may be taken to be the conductor M. Compare with EllipticCurveModularity's separately sourced proof via Serre's Theoreme 4.
Do not extend to number fields other than Q.

nodes.title: ACC+ Lemmas 7.1.5-7.1.8: decomposed genericity, enormous image and local shape of Hodge-Tate {0,1} crystalline representations, used to verify the residual hypotheses of Theorem 6.1.1
nodes.statement: (7.1.5) For a number field L and r: G_L -> GL_n(k) with k finite of characteristic l, if the normal closure M over Q of the field cut out by ad r contains no primitive l-th root of unity, then r is decomposed generic. (7.1.6) Let F/Q be finite with normal closure F~, m >= 1, l > 2m+3 prime, r: G_F -> GL_2(F-bar_l) with r(G_{F~}) ⊃ SL_2(F_l), and F'/F finite and linearly disjoint from F^{ker r-bar} over F. Then: (1) if l is unramified in F'/Q, ζ_l is not in F^{ker ad Sym^m r} F'; (2) (Sym^m r)(G_{F'(ζ_l)}) is enormous; (3) if ad r(G_{F~'}) ⊃ PSL_2(F_l), then Sym^m r|G_{F'} is decomposed generic; (4) the same if F'/Q is unramified at l and no quotient of im ad r is unramified at all primes above l; (5) if l > [F~:F], Sym^m r is decomposed generic. (7.1.7) Decomposed genericity and absolute irreducibility of r: G_F -> GL_n(F-bar_l) are preserved under restriction to G_{FE} for E/Q Galois and linearly disjoint from the Galois closure of F^{ker r}(ζ_l). (7.1.8) (1) For K/Q_l unramified and r: G_K -> GL_2(Z_l) crystalline with Hodge-Tate numbers {0,1} at every embedding, either r-bar|_{I_l}^ss ≅ 1 ⊕ ε-bar_l^{-1} or r-bar|_{I_l} ≅ ω_{l,2}^{-1} ⊕ ω_{l,2}^{-l}. (2) For K a number field with l unramified and r: G_K -> GL_2(Z_l) crystalline with Hodge-Tate numbers {0,1} and r-bar(G_K) ⊃ SL_2(F_l), the only subextension of K^{ker r-bar}/K unramified at all primes above l is K.
hypotheses: Lemma 7.1.6 needs l > 2m+3 and residual image containing SL_2(F_l) over the normal closure.

Lemma 7.1.8 has coefficients Z_l (not Z-bar_l). The source warns that (1) would be false for the ring of integers of an arbitrary extension of Q_l. This is why Assumption 7.2.6(1) makes l_2 split completely in each M_i before Lemma 7.1.8(1) is applied to r_{i,lambda_i}.

Lemma 7.1.8 is stated for every l, including l = 2. The proof of (1) treats l = 2 only by noting '1 = epsilon-bar_l^{-1}', and it invokes [Ray74, Prop. 3.2.1, Thm. 3.4.3] for a finite flat group scheme over the completed maximal unramified extension (e = 1). The text does not address whether Raynaud's e < p - 1 hypothesis holds at l = 2 (it does not: e = 1 = p - 1). nodes.title: ACC+ Corollary 7.2.4: potential automorphy of the symmetric powers of a non-CM elliptic curve over Q, over totally real fields, with avoidance and unramifiedness control
nodes.statement: Let M be a finite set of positive integers, E/Q a non-CM elliptic curve, L a finite set of rational primes at which E has good reduction, and F^avoid/Q a finite extension. Then there are a finite Galois extension F_2^avoid/Q, linearly disjoint from F^avoid over Q, and a finite totally real Galois extension F^suffices/Q, unramified above L and linearly disjoint from F^avoid F_2^avoid over Q, with the following property. For every finite totally real F'/F^suffices linearly disjoint from F_2^avoid over Q, and every m in M, there is a regular algebraic, cuspidal, polarizable automorphic representation pi of GL_{m+1}(A_{F'}) of weight (0)_{tau,i}. For some, hence every, prime l and ı: Qbar_l ≅ C, Sym^m r_{E,l}^dual|G_{F'} ≅ r_{l,ı}(pi). Moreover pi is unramified above every prime where E has good reduction.
hypotheses: E/Q has no CM; L is a finite set of primes of good reduction of E; M is a finite set of positive integers; F^avoid/Q is finite.
The extensions F' are totally real, contain F^suffices and are linearly disjoint from F_2^avoid over Q. Automorphy is not claimed over F^suffices-free fields or over Q.

The proof imports [BLGGT14] Theorems 2.4.1 and 3.1.2 (the latter in the strengthened form Proposition 7.2.3), Proposition 2.1.2, Lemmas A.2.5 and 2.2.4, and [CHT08, Lem. 4.2.2], and also Serre [Ser81, Th. 20] and [Ser72]. Of these, BLGGT14 Theorem 3.1.2 (with proof) and Theorem 2.4.1 (statement) are read in this stage's nodes and Lemma 2.2.4 was read as a statement; Proposition 2.1.2, Lemma A.2.5, [CHT08], [Ser81] and [Ser72] were not read.

Source gap (not closed in the text; errata register PAPER-ALLEN-ETAL-23/E105, awaiting review, and checked here against arXiv v2 pp. 205-208): Proposition 7.2.3 gives automorphy only over F_1 linearly disjoint from F^avoid F_1^avoid, and it is applied with F^avoid replaced by F^avoid L_3 and F_2^avoid := F_1^avoid L_3. The corollary's hypothesis, disjointness of F' from F_2^avoid alone, does not include disjointness from F^avoid. Either the corollary's hypothesis must be strengthened to disjointness from F^avoid F_2^avoid, or the proposition's weakened.
proofSteps: Choose a prime l >= max_{m in M} 2(m+2) with: E good ordinary at l; r-bar_{E,l} with image GL_2(F_l); l not in L; l unramified in F^avoid. Ordinarity excludes a density-zero set by [Ser81, Th. 20]; the other conditions exclude finitely many primes by [Ser72]. Qbar^{ker r-bar_{E,l}} contains zeta_l and is linearly disjoint from F^avoid (Lemma 7.1.8(2)).

Choose an imaginary quadratic L unramified at L, at the bad primes of E and at the primes ramified in F^avoid, and split at l. Choose q not in L ∪ {l}, split in L, unramified in F^avoid, of good reduction for E. For even m in M choose a character psi_m: G_L -> Qbar_l^x, crystalline above l with Hodge-Tate numbers 0 and m+1 at the two places above l, and with q | #(psi_m/psi_m^c)(G^nr_{F_{v_q}}). psi_m is unramified above L, above the primes ramified in F^avoid and above the bad primes of E, and satisfies psi_m psi_m^c = epsilon_l^{-(m+1)} ([BLGGT14, Lem. A.2.5]).

Form L_2, the compositum of the fields Q-bar^{ker Ind psi-bar_m} cut out by the residual inductions for m even (the source prints Ind^{G_L}_{G_Q} psi-bar_m there, with the groups interchanged), L_1 (its maximal subextension ramified only at l) and L_3 = L_2 Q-bar^{ker r-bar_{E,l}}. Show that F^avoid is linearly disjoint from L_3 over Q. Use the unique copy of SL_2(F_l) in Gal(M_1/(L_1 ∩ Q-bar^{ker r-bar})), normal in Gal(M_1/Q) with fixed field L_1(zeta_l), and the subgroup H generated by the inertia groups above l, which surjects onto Gal(Q-bar^{ker r-bar_{E,l}}/Q) by Lemma 7.1.8(2).

For odd m set r_m = Sym^m r_{E,l}^dual: G_Q -> GSp_{m+1}(Qbar_l), with multiplier epsilon_l^{-m}, crystalline ordinary at l with Hodge-Tate numbers {0,...,m}. For even m set r_m = Sym^m r_{E,l}^dual ⊗ Ind_{G_L}^{G_Q} psi_m: G_Q -> GSp_{2(m+1)}, with multiplier epsilon_l^{-(2m+1)} and Hodge-Tate numbers {0,...,2m+1}. The displayed formula on p. 1102 writes Ind_{G_F}^{G_Q} psi_m, but psi_m is a character of G_L and p. 1101 writes Ind_{G_L}^{G_Q}; the G_F is read as a misprint (checked on the page image).

nodes.title: ACC+ Theorem 7.1.11 (main potential automorphy theorem): symmetric powers of strongly irreducible rank-2 weight-{0,1} very weakly compatible systems become automorphic over controlled CM extensions
nodes.statement: Let F/F_0 be a finite Galois extension of CM fields, F_0^avoid/F a finite Galois extension, and L_0 a finite set of rational primes. Let I be a finite set, and for i in I let m_i in Z_{>0} and R_i = (M_i, S_i, {Q_{i,v}(X)}, {r_{i,lambda}}, {{0,1}}) be a strongly irreducible rank-2 very weakly compatible system of l-adic representations of G_F with S_i disjoint from L_0. Then there are: a finite set L ⊃ L_0 of rational primes; a finite CM Galois extension F^suffices/F, unramified above L and Galois over F_0; and a finite Galois extension F^avoid/F containing F_0^avoid and linearly disjoint from F^suffices over F. They have the following property. For every finite CM extension F'/F containing F^suffices, unramified above L and linearly disjoint from F^avoid over F, the representations Sym^{m_i} R_i|G_{F'} are all automorphic, and each arises from an automorphic representation unramified above L_0. Corollary 7.1.12 is the special case of a single system: there is a finite Galois CM extension F'/F with Sym^m R|G_{F'} automorphic. The theorem is potential automorphy only. It gives automorphy over F' and no descent to F.
hypotheses: F/F_0 is a finite Galois extension of CM fields; F_0^avoid/F is finite Galois; L_0 is a finite set of rational primes.

Each R_i is a rank-2, strongly irreducible, very weakly compatible system in the sense of ACC+ §7.1, with Hodge-Tate multisets {0,1} at all embeddings. 'Very weakly compatible' requires crystallinity with the given Hodge-Tate numbers only for l outside a Dirichlet density zero set.
S_i ∩ L_0 = ∅ for all i.

The proof applies ACC+ Theorem 6.1.1 (Fontaine-Laffaille automorphy lifting for n-dimensional representations of an imaginary CM or totally real F; statement on arXiv v2 pp. 132-133, page image checked). Its hypotheses: rho unramified almost everywhere; crystalline at v | p with p unramified in F; rho-bar absolutely irreducible and decomposed generic; rho-bar(G_{F(zeta_p)}) enormous; a sigma in G_F - G_{F(zeta_p)} with rho-bar(sigma) scalar; p > n^2; and a cuspidal pi, regular algebraic of weight lambda with lambda_{tau,1} + lambda_{tau c,1} - lambda_{tau,n} - lambda_{tau c,n} < p - 2n, with rho-bar ≅ r-bar_iota(pi), HT_tau(rho) = {lambda_{iota tau,1} + n - 1, ..., lambda_{iota tau,n}}, and pi_v unramified for v | p.

Source gap (verified here; also errata register PAPER-ALLEN-ETAL-23/E106, awaiting review): Theorem 6.1.1 is applied with n = m_i + 1 at p = l_1 and p = l_2 and needs p > (m_i + 1)^2, while Assumption 7.2.6(6) arranges only l_1, l_2 > 2m_i + 3; for m_i >= 3 this is weaker (m_i = 3 allows l = 11, 13 < 16). Lemma 7.1.8(1) and Theorem 6.1.1(2) also need r_{i,lambda_i} crystalline with Hodge-Tate numbers {0,1} above l_2, which very weak compatibility gives only outside a density-zero set and Assumption 7.2.6 does not list. Both extra conditions exclude a density-zero set, so the choice of l_1, l_2 remains possible.

Source gap: Step 8 applies Corollary 7.2.4, which is stated for totally real F', to the CM field F'. The passage through the maximal totally real subfield of F' (which contains F^{+,suffices}), its disjointness from F_2^avoid, and quadratic base change to F' is not written in the source (arXiv v2 p. 211).
proofSteps: §7.2.5 step 1: choose a non-CM elliptic curve E/Q with good reduction above L_0, distinct primes l_1, l_2, and lambda_i | l_2, satisfying Assumption 7.2.6. The conditions are: l_2 splits completely in each M_i; the image of G_F on E[l_1] contains SL_2(F_{l_1}) and r-bar_{i,lambda_i}(G_F) ⊃ SL_2(F_{l_2}); l_1, l_2 are unramified in F; E has good reduction above l_1, l_2; l_1, l_2 lie under no prime of any S_i; l_1, l_2 > 2m_i + 3. All but the first hold for a density-one set by Lemma 7.1.3; the first holds for a positive-density set. Put L = L_0 ∪ {l_1, l_2}.

Step 2 (determinant twist): det r_{i,lambda} = psi_i epsilon_l^{-1}, with psi_i of finite order and unramified outside S_i. The obstruction ∂psi_i in Br_F[2] is non-trivial only at places in S_i. Choose a soluble Galois totally real F_1^+/Q with these properties: unramified above L; linearly disjoint from the normal closure F_1^avoid of F_0^avoid F^{ker(r-bar_{E,l_1} × ∏ r-bar_{i,lambda_i})}; inertia degrees at p_v divisible by 2[F_v:Q_{p_v}] for v in ∪S_i ([CHT08, Lem. 4.1.2]). Then psi_i|G_{FF_1^+} = phi_i^2, and by Grunwald-Wang ([AT09, Ch. X, Th. 5]) one may take phi_i unramified above L. Set R'_i = R_i|G_{FF_1^+} ⊗ phi_i^{-1}.
Step 3: apply Corollary 7.2.4 to {m_i}, E, L and F_1^avoid F_1^+, obtaining F_2^avoid and F^{+,suffices}. Put F^avoid = F_1^avoid F_2^avoid.

Step 4 (auxiliary moduli): give the space V of the residual r-bar'_{i,lambda_i} a symplectic pairing, preserved up to the multiplier epsilon-bar_{l_2}^{-1}. Let Y_i/FF_1^+ be the moduli space of elliptic curves D with symplectic isomorphisms alpha_1: E[l_1] ≅ D[l_1] and alpha_2: V^dual ≅ D[l_2], and let X_i/F^+F_1^+ be its restriction of scalars. X_i has points at the infinite places. At places w above L_0 ∪ {l_1}, some f >= 1 gives r-bar'_{i,lambda_i}(Frob_w)^{-f} ~ r-bar_{E,l_2}(Frob_w)^f. Then E gives a point of Y_i, with good reduction, over the unramified extension of degree f.

Step 5 (points above l_2): since Q_{l_2} ≅ M_{i,lambda_i} (Assumption 7.2.6(1)), Lemma 7.1.8(1) applies, and r-bar'_{i,lambda_i}|G_{(F_1^+F)_w} is either (1) induced from the unramified quadratic extension of omega_{l_2,2}^{-1} delta, or (2) an extension of chi^{-1} epsilon-bar^{-1} by chi, with chi unramified and a peu ramifié class in H^1_f. The source asserts that the direction of the extension and the peu ramifié property 'follow easily from the connected-étale sequence' for the group scheme H of Lemma 7.1.8; this is not written out. In case (1), take D with good supersingular reduction and f with r-bar_{E,l_1}(Frob_v)^{2f} = (-l_2)^f mod l_1. D gives a point over the unramified extension of degree 2f. In case (2), take an ordinary D over k(w) and use Serre-Tate theory: lifts are parametrised by H^1(G_L, Z_{l_2}(epsilon psi^{-2})) = H^1_f. Lemma 7.2.2 (surjectivity of H^1_f(G_L, Z_l(epsilon chi)) -> H^1_f(G_L, F_l(epsilon-bar chi-bar))) gives a lift D_e with D_e[l_1] ≅ E[l_1] and r-bar_{D_e,l_2} ≅ (r-bar'_{i,lambda_i})^dual.

Step 6 (global points): 'for instance, by [BLGGT14, Prop. 3.1.1]' there is a totally real F_2^+/F_1^+F^+ with these properties: Galois over F_0^+; all primes above L unramified in F_2^+/F^+, with each D_i of good reduction there; linearly disjoint over F_1^+F^+ from F^avoid F^{+,suffices} F_1^+; ∏ X_i has an F_2^+-point. That is, there are elliptic curves D_i over F_2 with D_i[l_1] ≅ E[l_1]|G_{F_2} and D_i[l_2] ≅ r-bar'_{i,lambda_i}|^dual_{G_{F_2}}.
Step 7: set F^suffices = F^{+,suffices} F_2^+ F and verify its linear disjointness from F^avoid over F (the field diagram on p. 1106).

Step 8: for F' as in the statement, Corollary 7.2.4 is invoked to give pi_i of weight (0), unramified above L, with Sym^{m_i} r_{E,l_1}^dual|G_{F'} ≅ r_{l_1,ı}(pi_i) (F' is CM here while the corollary is stated for totally real fields; see the gap). Theorem 6.1.1, with the residual conditions supplied by parts (1), (2) and (4) of Lemma 7.1.6 together with Lemma 7.1.8 (which has only two parts), transfers automorphy at l_1 to Sym^{m_i} r_{D_i,l_1}^dual|G_{F'}. Hence it holds at l_2 by compatibility, and Theorem 6.1.1 again transfers it to Sym^{m_i} r'_{i,lambda_i}|G_{F'}. Untwisting by phi_i completes the proof.

nodes.title: BLGGT14 Proposition 3.1.1: a Moret-Bailly point-existence theorem with prescribed local Galois extensions, Galois closure over K_0 and linear disjointness
nodes.statement: Let K^(avoid)/K/K_0 be number fields with K^(avoid)/K and K/K_0 Galois. Let S be a finite set of places of K_0, and S_K the places of K above S. For v in S_K let L'_v/K_v be a finite Galois extension with L'_{σv} = σL'_v for σ in G_{K_{0,v|K_0}} (the decomposition group of K_0 at the place below v). Let T/K be a smooth, geometrically connected variety, and for each v in S_K let Ω_v ⊂ T(L'_v) be a non-empty Gal(L'_v/K_v)-invariant open subset. Then there are a finite Galois extension L/K and a point P in T(L) such that: L/K_0 is Galois; L/K is linearly disjoint from K^(avoid)/K; for v in S_K and w | v a prime of L, L_w/K_v ≅ L'_v/K_v and P ∈ Ω_v ⊂ T(L'_v) ≅ T(L_w).
hypotheses: T is smooth and geometrically connected over K (not K_0), and each Ω_v is non-empty, open and Gal(L'_v/K_v)-invariant.
The local extensions L'_v are Galois and compatible with the G_{K_0}-action on S_K.

nodes.title: Newton-Thorne I Theorem 8.1 (Theorem B): Sym^{n-1} automorphy for non-CM forms of weight >= 2 whose local components all have non-trivial Jacquet module
nodes.statement: Let pi be a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(A_Q) of weight k >= 2 such that (1) for each prime l, pi_l has non-trivial Jacquet module (equivalently, pi_l has an accessible refinement, i.e. is not supercuspidal), and (2) pi is not CM. Then for every n >= 3 and every iota: Qbar_p -> C, Sym^{n-1} r_{pi,iota} is automorphic. Examples include non-CM eigenforms of level Gamma_1(N) with N squarefree, in particular semistable elliptic curves over Q when k = 2 (Corollary C: Λ(Sym^n E, s) is entire for semistable E).

proofSteps: Proposition 8.2 (induction on the number r of primes dividing the conductor N; base r = 0 is Theorem 7.7). Hypothesis: every ramified l has an n-regular accessible refinement, and pi is non-CM. For a ramified p write N = M p^s. If r_{pi,iota}|G_{Q_p} is reducible, pi is iota-ordinary. On the tame-level-M p-adic eigencurve, avoiding the Zariski-closed set Z of Lemma 2.35, find an ordinary classical pi' on the same component with: level prime to p; n-regular refinements at l | M; Zariski closure ⊃ SL_2. By induction Sym^{n-1} r_{pi'} is automorphic; the ordinary case of Theorem 2.33 gives Sym^{n-1} r_pi. The locally irreducible case is identical, using a non-ordinary numerically non-critical n-regular refinement and Lemma 3.5.

Proposition 8.3 (reduction to 8.2). Choose p > max(2(n+1), (n-1)k) with image of r-bar_{pi,iota} ⊃ SL_2(F_p), pi_p unramified, and formally smooth fixed-determinant local lifting rings at ramified l ≠ p. Choose an auxiliary q_a. Set up Taylor-Wiles-Kisin patching for H = H^1(Y_{U_1(Mq_a)}, Sym^{k-2} O^2)_m, with Fontaine-Laffaille condition at p and all lifts at l in S.

Lemma 8.4: for l in S - {p} there is a principal ideal I_l ⊂ R_l cutting out the lifts whose Frobenius eigenvalue ratio is a root of unity of order <= n-1, and dim R_l/I_l < dim R_l. Take I_l generated by the discriminant of the characteristic polynomial of Sym^{n-1} r_l^univ(phi_l). It is non-zero: in the Steinberg case by the eigenvalue ratio; otherwise by an explicit deformation and [Gee11, Prop. 2.1.5].

If every automorphic pi' contributing to H_{Q_N} failed n-regularity at some ramified l, then I·H^T_{Q_N} = 0. Patching would give H_∞ finite free over S_∞ (dimension 4|T| + q_0) but supported on R_∞ = (A^T_S/I)[[X_1..X_g]] of dimension 4|T| + q_0 - 1, a contradiction by [KT17, Lemma 2.8]. So some congruent pi' is n-regular at every ramified l. At q in Q_N, r_{pi'}|I_q = C_q ⊕ C_q^{-1} with p-power order and p > 2n, which is n-regular.

Proof of Theorem 8.1: take p, iota, pi' from Proposition 8.3. Sym^{n-1} r_{pi'} is automorphic by Proposition 8.2. Sym^{n-1} r-bar_{pi,iota} ≅ Sym^{n-1} r-bar_{pi',iota} is irreducible, so [BLGGT14, Theorem 4.2.1] gives automorphy of Sym^{n-1} r_{pi,iota}.

nodes.title: Status of Arthur's and Mok's endoscopic classification after AGIKMS: conditional only on the twisted weighted fundamental lemma
nodes.statement: Status statement, as established by AGIKMS (arXiv v3, 2026). The main theorems of Arthur's book [Ar3] (quasi-split symplectic and special orthogonal groups) and of Mok [Mok] (quasi-split unitary groups) are proved by a simultaneous induction on N. They comprise: local classification (Theorems 1.5.1, 2.2.1, 2.2.4); local intertwining relations (2.4.1, 2.4.4); global seed theorems (1.4.1, 1.4.2); global classification (1.5.2, 1.5.3); stable multiplicity formulas (4.1.2, 4.2.2). These theorems relied on unproven assertions. [A24] is resolved by Mœglin-Waldspurger [MW4, I.4.11]. [A25], [A26], [A27] are supplied by AGIKMS's Main Theorems 3, 2, 1, together with Appendices D (Arthur's Lemma 2.5.5) and E (archimedean endoscopic character relations). The one remaining hypothesis is the twisted weighted fundamental lemma [MW4, II.4.4], on which the stabilisation of the twisted trace formula [MW4, MW5] depends. Consequently the classification for quasi-split classical groups becomes unconditional once the twisted weighted fundamental lemma is verified. [KMSW] and [Ish] extend it only partially to non-quasi-split groups.
hypotheses: Groups: quasi-split symplectic, special orthogonal (Arthur) and unitary (Mok) groups over number fields and their local fields of characteristic zero.

The twisted weighted fundamental lemma is an explicit hypothesis. It reduces via [W4, Theorem 3.8] to (i) the weighted fundamental lemma for Lie algebras and (ii) its non-standard version. (i) is proved for split groups by Chaudouard-Laumon; no written proof of (i) for non-split groups or of (ii) exists as of AGIKMS v3.
The unweighted fundamental lemma in all versions is a theorem (Ngô, Waldspurger and others).
The proofs of AGIKMS's main theorems (§§2-7 and Appendices A-F) and of [Ar3], [Mok], [MW4], [MW5] were not read.
proofSteps: AGIKMS §0.1 organises Arthur's main theorems into local classification, local intertwining relations, global seed, global classification and stable multiplicity formula groups. They are proved simultaneously by induction on N for twisted endoscopic groups of GL_N.
§0.3: [A24] justified [Ar3, Proposition 2.1.1] (choosing test functions on twisted GL_N amounts to compatible families on twisted endoscopic groups). It is proved in general by [MW4, I.4.11].

§0.2.1: Main Theorem 1 (Theorem 1.8.1) proves [Ar3, Theorem 2.5.1(b)] (deferred to [A27]) by comparing Arthur's normalising factors with Shahidi's local coefficients (§2, Appendix A). Appendix D proves [Ar3, Lemma 2.5.5]. With Appendix E, this makes [Ar3, Chapter 6] conditional only on the twisted weighted fundamental lemma.

§0.2: Main Theorem 2 (Theorem 1.9.1) is [Ar3, Theorem 2.5.3], deferred to [A26]; Main Theorem 3 corresponds to [A25] ([Ar3, Lemma 7.1.2]) and includes the construction of co-tempered A-packets by Aubert duality, used in Step 1 of Arthur's Chapter 7.
§0.4: stabilisation of the twisted trace formula depends on [MW4, II.4.4], which remains conditional; it reduces to (i) and (ii). A full proof of (i) and (ii) is in progress ([HD]).
acceptance: Any consumer (for example Galois representations for torsion classes over totally real fields via Sp_2n) must carry the twisted weighted fundamental lemma as an explicit hypothesis.
Record separately that ET.3 and ET.4 (the simple stable and twisted unitary trace comparison route) do not supply the stabilised twisted trace formula needed here.

nodes.statement: Let E/F be a quadratic extension of fields of characteristic zero and U_{E/F}(N) the quasi-split unitary group. Theorem 2.5.1 (F local): (a) for every local A-parameter ψ there is a finite multiset Π_ψ with a canonical map π -> <.,π> to the character group of S-bar_ψ, trivial when U_{E/F}(N) and π are unramified, and consisting of irreducible unitary representations; (b) for bounded generic ψ = φ, Π_φ is multiplicity free and tempered, the map to the character group is injective (bijective for non-archimedean F), and the tempered dual is the disjoint union of the Π_φ (the local Langlands classification for U_{E/F}(N)); (c) central characters are given by det ψ^N. Theorem 2.5.2 (F global): for κ = ±1 and χ_κ, L^2_disc(U_{E/F}(N)(F) \ U_{E/F}(N)(A_F)) = ⊕_{ψ in Ψ_2(U_{E/F}(N), ξ_{χ_κ})} ⊕_{π in Π_ψ(ε_ψ)} π, where Π_ψ(ε_ψ) is the set of π in the global packet with <.,π> = ε_ψ, Arthur's sign character. Remark 2.5.3 gives multiplicity one for generic parameters. Theorem 2.5.4: (a) for a conjugate self-dual simple generic φ^N, L(s, φ^N, Asai^η) has a pole at s = 1 with η = (-1)^{N-1} κ; (b) for conjugate self-dual simple φ_1, φ_2 of the same parity, ε(1/2, φ_1 × (φ_2)^c) = 1. As in Arthur's work, these theorems are proved by one long induction completed at the end of the paper. Mok states that the results remain conditional on the stabilization of the twisted trace formula.

nodes.title: The conditional implication SP_r + SP_{p-r} + LR_{p+r} + TP_r ⇒ SP_{p+r} and what is known of TP and LR, as recorded by Newton-Thorne (Hilbert)
nodes.statement: As recorded in the introduction of Newton-Thorne (Hilbert), for a totally real field F. SP_n (Conjecture B) is the existence, for all non-CM cuspidal regular algebraic pi of GL_2(A_F), of Sym^{n-1} pi as a RAESDC representation. TP_r is a conjecture on the existence of a certain instance of GL_2 ⊗ GL_r -> GL_2r tensor product functoriality. LR_{p+r} is a conjecture on level-raising congruences in degree p+r. Clozel-Thorne [CT14] proved the implication (1.2): SP_r + SP_{p-r} + LR_{p+r} + TP_r ⇒ SP_{p+r}, for p prime and 0 < r < p. [CT15, CT17] then proved SP_n for n <= 9 under mild technical hypotheses on F. [Tho24] proved all required LR_n, so that TP_r for all r implies SP_n for all n; with the known TP_r this gives SP_n for n <= 9 and even n <= 26. Newton-Thorne (Hilbert) proves SP_n for all n by establishing just enough tensor product functoriality (residual automorphy of phi_p r-bar ⊗ Sym^{r-1} r-bar), not TP_r in general.
hypotheses: F totally real; pi non-CM, cuspidal, regular algebraic.
